The [labour productivity](/wiki/Workforce_productivity "Workforce productivity") level of Luxembourg is one of the highest in Europe. [OECD](/wiki/OECD "OECD"), 2012.

[Luxembourg](/wiki/Luxembourg "Luxembourg") has a [developed economy](/wiki/Developed_country "Developed country") largely dependent on the banking, steel, and industrial sectors. Citizens of Luxembourg enjoy the highest [per capita gross domestic product](/wiki/Lists_of_countries_by_GDP_per_capita "Lists of countries by GDP per capita") in the world, according to an [IMF](/wiki/International_Monetary_Fund "International Monetary Fund") estimate in 2022.[[26]](#cite_note-IMF-26) Among [OECD](/wiki/OECD "OECD") nations, Luxembourg has a highly efficient and strong [social security system](/wiki/Social_welfare_in_Luxembourg "Social welfare in Luxembourg"); social welfare expenditure stood at [roughly 21.9% of GDP](/wiki/Welfare_state#Effects "Welfare state").[[3]](#cite_note-Kenworthy-3)[[4]](#cite_note-Bradley_et_al.-4)[[27]](#cite_note-27)

Prior to the mid-19th century, Luxembourg was primarily rural and mostly isolated from commerce with neighboring economies.[[28]](#cite_note-:2-28) In the late 19th century, Luxembourg's dominant sector was steel industry.[[28]](#cite_note-:2-28) Over time, the main economic sector became finance.[[29]](#cite_note-:3-29) Due to its reputation for secrecy, it has become an attractive location for individuals and businesses to hold assets for tax avoidance and tax evasion purposes.[[30]](#cite_note-:4-30)[[31]](#cite_note-31)

On November 23, 2014, Mallett tore his pectoral muscle and Fitzpatrick was renamed the starter.[[60]](#cite_note-60) During a Week 13 45–21 victory over the [Tennessee Titans](/wiki/2014_Tennessee_Titans_season "2014 Tennessee Titans season"), Fitzpatrick threw for 358 yards and a franchise-record six touchdowns and 358 yards for a 147.5 [passer rating](/wiki/Passer_rating "Passer rating").[[61]](#cite_note-61) He earned AFC Offensive Player of the Week honors for his performance against the Titans.[[62]](#cite_note-62) Two weeks later against the [Indianapolis Colts](/wiki/2014_Indianapolis_Colts_season "2014 Indianapolis Colts season"), Fitzpatrick scrambled for a two-yard gain in the second quarter, was tripped up, and left the eventual 17–10 loss with a fractured left tibia, ending his season. Fitzpatrick was replaced by rookie [Tom Savage](/wiki/Tom_Savage_(American_football) "Tom Savage (American football)"), who also received a minor injury.[[63]](#cite_note-63)

Fitzpatrick finished 2014 the season with 2,483 passing yards, 17 touchdowns, and eight interceptions for a then career-high 95.3 passer rating to go along with 50 carries for 184 yards and two touchdowns and a 6–6 record as the starting quarterback for the Texans.[[64]](#cite_note-64)

Eswatini has a spectrum of formal and informal conservation areas that protect the nation's rich biological diversity. These areas comprise about 5% of the country's land area. This diversity suggests Eswatini is globally important for biodiversity conservation.[[74]](#cite_note-BSAP-78) Land degradation and conversion to other land uses are the major threats to biodiversity, including plantation agriculture (legal and illegal), bush-clearing, the spread of alien and invasive plants, and unsustainable resource harvesting; major land fragmentation is evident.[[74]](#cite_note-BSAP-78)

Eswatini is a signatory to the [Convention on Biological Diversity](/wiki/Convention_on_Biological_Diversity "Convention on Biological Diversity"), the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species ([CITES](/wiki/CITES "CITES")), and the United National Framework Convention on Climate Change. There are three main government ministries responsible for national biodiversity management: the Eswatini National Trust Commission, the [Eswatini Environment Authority](/wiki/Eswatini_Environment_Authority "Eswatini Environment Authority"), and the Ministry of Agriculture and Cooperatives. After the 2022–23 season ended, the organization began a complete overhaul of the front office. On May 11, 2023, the team hired former Flyer [Keith Jones](/wiki/Keith_Jones_(ice_hockey) "Keith Jones (ice hockey)") as president of hockey operations and named Daniel Briere as permanent general manager of the team.[[68]](#cite_note-71) Soon after the team fired longtime player development coaches [Kjell Samuelsson](/wiki/Kjell_Samuelsson "Kjell Samuelsson") and John Riley, as well as senior advisor [Mike O'Connell](/wiki/Mike_O%27Connell "Mike O'Connell").[[69]](#cite_note-72) The front office overhaul was accompanied by uniform changes, with the team branding it as a "New Era of Orange".[[70]](#cite_note-73)

The first major move of the Jones/Briere era came in the [2023 entry draft](/wiki/2023_NHL_entry_draft "2023 NHL entry draft") when the Flyers selected Russian prospect [Matvei Michkov](/wiki/Matvei_Michkov "Matvei Michkov") with the seventh overall pick. However, Michkov had already been signed to a contract with [SKA Saint Petersburg](/wiki/SKA_Saint_Petersburg "SKA Saint Petersburg") of the [Kontinental Hockey League](/wiki/Kontinental_Hockey_League "Kontinental Hockey League") (KHL) for another three seasons, and his time of arrival to the NHL was still unknown.[[71]](#cite_note-74)

Despite low expectations amid the rebuild, the Flyers remained in playoff contention well into the [2023–24 season](/wiki/2023%E2%80%9324_NHL_season "2023–24 NHL season"). On March 23, 2024, the team held a record of 36–26–9 while four points up on the third playoff spot in the Metropolitan Division. However, a collapse ensued as the Flyers won just two of their last 11 games to miss the playoffs for the fourth consecutive season.[[72]](#cite_note-75) A major development occurred in the middle of the 2023–24 season when Carter Hart, thought to be the franchise goaltender of the future for the Flyers, took an indefinite leave from the team after being named as a suspect in the [Hockey Canada sexual assault scandal](/wiki/Hockey_Canada_sexual_assault_scandal "Hockey Canada sexual assault scandal").
